events.title: Contemporáneo 1. Materia :: Alquimia :: Dispositivo :: Flujo
events.description: A long-running exhibition of contemporary art from the MAC Lima collection, in Sala 3 of the Barranco museum.

events.title: El tejido como memoria. Centro de Textiles Tradicionales del Cusco
events.description: Work by Cusco weavers carrying on textile techniques passed down through generations, presented as living Andean heritage.

events.description: An exhibition, curated by Kristel Best, on poet and activist Magda Portal from the 1920s to 1980 — first editions, periodicals and photographs of her avant-garde and social poetry. Housed in a colonial-era mansion in the historic centre.

events.title: Desde Adentro (Ricardo Inga Arizola)

events.title: Una mirada británica: Kate Hepburn, 60 años de arte y diseño

events.title: Sobreviviendo en azul y tierra (Erika Humala)

events.title: Sueño

events.title: La mujer de negro (The Woman in Black)

events.title: Leo Middea

events.description: Baltimore Heritage walk exploring John Wilkes Booth's Baltimore roots, Civil War Baltimore and the plots against Lincoln, ending at Booth's unmarked grave.

events.description: Two-hour evening walking tour of Lima's 1808 cemetery-museum, mixing city history with ghost stories, with stops at pavilions, crypts and mausoleums. Registration at Gate 1 by 7:30 pm (ends about 9:30 pm); the with-transport option meets at 6:20 pm by the Casa Matusita.
events.summary: Spanish-language. Teleticket lists the run through Dec 20 but not individual session dates; resellers indicate Friday and Saturday nights. Confirm a session before going.
events.source: Teleticket listing; Experiencias.com.pe and Atrápalo for schedule pattern

events.title: Tatiana Figueroa Ramírez: "Exhume"
events.description: Book talk for Tatiana Figueroa Ramírez's "Exhume," about women's legacies, in conversation with Maryland State Poet Laureate Lady Brion.

events.title: Ben Gucciardi with Edgar Kunz & Samuel Cheney: "Arguments"
events.description: Poetry reading from Ben Gucciardi's collection "Arguments," with Baltimore poets Edgar Kunz and Samuel Cheney reading their own work.

events.title: Benjamin Robert Siegel: "Markets of Pain"
events.description: Historian Benjamin Robert Siegel talks about the history of the legal opium trade from his book "Markets of Pain," in conversation with Alicia Puglionesi and Devin Hernandez.

events.title: Waterfall Dances: Jane Goodall in memoriam
events.description: Organist Douglas Buchanan plays nature-inspired works honoring Jane Goodall, a year after her death, in St. David's Church, Roland Park.

events.title: Historic Green Mount Cemetery (Baltimore Heritage tour)
events.description: A Baltimore Heritage walking tour of the 1839 park-style cemetery where many notable Marylanders are buried. Uneven grass and cobblestones.

events.title: Patterson Park (Baltimore Heritage tour)
events.address: 28 S Patterson Park Ave, Baltimore, MD 21231
events.description: A walk through Patterson Park's history, from its 1827 founding through its wartime roles and its growth to 137 acres.

events.title: Nemanja Radulović & Double Sens: The Four Seasons
events.description: Serbian violinist Nemanja Radulović and his ensemble Double Sens play Vivaldi's Four Seasons in recital.

events.title: Hoodstock XXIII
events.description: A grassroots music-festival fundraiser for Unified Community Connections at the Baltimore Museum of Industry, with live music, food, drinks, raffles and a silent auction.

events.title: Jonestown: A Walking Tour (Baltimore Heritage)
events.description: Guide Bev Rosen leads a tour of one of Baltimore's oldest neighborhoods, highlighting its Eastern European Jewish heritage and early landmarks like the McKim Free School and Lloyd Street Synagogue.

events.title: Brewer's Hill: Where Immigrants Brewed a Community (Baltimore Heritage)
events.description: A one-mile walk through a former farming area that became an immigrant brewing neighborhood: its rowhouses and breweries like National Bohemian and Gunther.

events.title: Celtic Recital & Evensong
events.description: The Choir of St. David's sings with Celtic harpist Liv Castor for the feast of St. Margaret of Scotland.

events.title: Hélène Grimaud (Shriver Hall Concert Series)
events.description: French pianist Hélène Grimaud plays Beethoven's and Schubert's final piano sonatas.

events.title: Historic Green Mount Cemetery (Baltimore Heritage tour)
events.description: A Baltimore Heritage walking tour of the 1839 park-style cemetery and its notable burials. Runs rain or shine.

events.title: Artemis: Sketches of Miles
events.description: The all-star quintet Artemis — Renee Rosnes, Ingrid Jensen, Nicole Glover, Noriko Ueda, Allison Miller — marks Miles Davis's centennial with modal-era and electric-era arrangements alongside originals. DownBeat readers' #1 jazz group 2023–25.
events.summary: Fri Dec 11 & Sat Dec 12.

events.title: Booth, Baltimore & Lincoln's Assassination: Green Mount walking tour
events.description: A walk tracing John Wilkes Booth's Baltimore roots and the plots against Lincoln, ending at Booth's unmarked grave in Green Mount Cemetery.

events.title: Zbigniew Zukowski: Opening Reception
events.description: Opening for an exhibition of mixed-media work by Polish-American artist Zbigniew Zukowski; the artist is on hand to talk about the work.

events.title: Nina Gala: Nothing Is Like It Was Before
events.description: Singer-songwriter Nina Gala performs inside Mount Vernon Place United Methodist Church during Emma Childs's Chora installation.

events.title: Wondering & Wandering: Photo Workshop
events.description: Three-hour hands-on street-photography workshop walking Highlandtown, learning to notice patterns and capture city life. Led by Lyon, a Baltimore photographer and designer who teaches at MICA, UMBC and BSA; bring a phone or a camera on auto. All skill levels.

events.title: Mother Earth Poetry Vibe featuring FreeQuency
events.description: Red Emma's Mother Earth Poetry Vibe reading series, this edition featuring the poet FreeQuency.

events.title: Profs & Pints: How Ancient Athens Restored Democracy
events.description: Nicholas D. Cross, a U.S. Naval Academy historian, explains how Athenians rebuilt a divided community after the rule of the Thirty Tyrants. Doors 3 p.m.

events.title: BSO: Shéhérazade & Sibelius
events.description: The Baltimore Symphony Orchestra and music director Jonathon Heyward with mezzo-soprano Fleur Barron in Ravel's Shéhérazade song cycle, plus Sibelius.

events.title: Girl Island: The Sandy Stone Story
events.description: Trans Awareness Month evening around Girl Island, the documentary on Sandy Stone, the trans pioneer, recording engineer and media theorist, with screenings, food, drink, conversation and dancing; the 89-year-old Stone is the guest of honor. 20% of proceeds go to Maryland Safe Haven.

events.title: See It Loud: The Globe Poster Story (World Premiere)
events.description: World premiere of John Lewis and Rei Perri's hour-long documentary on Baltimore's Globe Poster and its influence on music, design and pop culture, with interviews with musicians who commissioned the posters, the printers who made them, and the MICA folks carrying on the tradition. Afterward: original Globe posters for sale from the Cicero Archive and the Globe exhibition in the Pinkard Gallery.
events.summary: Doors 6:30 p.m. Super Fan tickets add early shopping of the Cicero Archive, 5–6:45 p.m.

events.title: Globe Posters for the People
events.description: Near-centennial retrospective of Globe Poster, the Baltimore printer behind showcard posters for musicians, political campaigns, rodeos and circuses, drawn from an archive of more than 15,000 items now owned by MICA.
events.summary: Mon–Fri 10–5, Sun 12–6.

events.title: Alice Miranda Ollstein: Side Effects
events.description: Health-policy journalist Alice Miranda Ollstein presents Side Effects: How Abortion Bans Impact Everyone's Health, in conversation with Jaisal Noor.

events.title: Shawn Gude: American Socialist (Eugene V. Debs)
events.description: Shawn Gude presents American Socialist: The Life and Legacy of Eugene V. Debs, a biography of the labor leader and five-time presidential candidate, in conversation with Johns Hopkins political scientist Lester Spence.

events.title: Gardener's Workshop: Gardening in Late Fall
events.description: Cylburn Arboretum Friends horticulture staff lead an interactive tour of the grounds with live demonstrations of November garden practices. Meet at the Nature Education Center porch behind the mansion; bring garden gloves.

events.title: Profs & Pints: How to Feel Worthy
events.description: Psychologist and author Marisa G. Franco gives an interactive talk on self-worth and shifting long-held negative beliefs about yourself. Doors 5 p.m.

events.title: The Stars: Andrew Schneider
events.description: Immersive LED-and-sound installation by Andrew Schneider at the Voxel in Remington.
events.summary: Times vary; book a slot on the Voxel site.

events.title: Priya Parker: The Art of Fighting
events.description: Priya Parker, author of The Art of Gathering, talks about navigating conflict, drawing on her new book The Art of Fighting.

events.title: An Evening of Literature and Music
events.description: Readings and music at Black Cherry with Lee Bains III, Baltimore writer Baynard Woods, Eze Jackson and Papess. Doors 6:30 p.m.

events.title: Puppet Slamwich
events.description: Black Cherry's adults-only evening of short puppetry acts: Alex Hart & Annajane, Schroeder Cherry and His Puppets, Leave No Trace, Fox e. Martin, Convulsionistas and Sari Langholt, hosted by musical guest Makeshift Hammer.
events.summary: Two shows, 6:30 and 9:30 p.m.; doors 30 min before.

events.title: 47th Annual Saturday with Sherlock Holmes
events.venue: Enoch Pratt Central Library, Wheeler Auditorium
events.description: Baltimore's long-running gathering of Sherlockians: presenters give talks on the Holmes stories, this year on the theme "International Holmes." Coffee and bagels 10:30, program 11:30–1:30.

events.title: Evergreen Holiday Makers' Market
events.description: Local makers sell their work at the Garrett family's Gilded Age mansion, followed by a self-guided tour of the museum and gardens.

events.title: Rodrigo Nunes: Anatomy of Disintegration
events.description: Philosopher Rodrigo Nunes presents Anatomy of Disintegration: What Brazil Reveals About the Global Far Right, in conversation with Mike McGuire.

events.title: Baseball in Baltimore: A Walking Tour
events.description: Baltimore Heritage walk from Babe Ruth's birthplace covering Ruth's early life in Baltimore, Brooks Robinson's career and the city's Negro Leagues history.

events.title: Baker Artist Awards Live!
events.description: Live presentation of the Baker Artist Awards, the yearly prizes for Baltimore-area artists, at Creative Alliance's Patterson theater.

events.title: Profs & Pints: The Power of Cults
events.description: George Mason psychologist Mariah Wilkerson on how cults recruit, how they keep members from leaving, and why leaving is so hard. Doors 5 p.m.

events.title: Meg Berkobien & María Cristina Hall: Goodbye, Ramona
events.description: Meg Berkobien and María Cristina Hall present the book Goodbye, Ramona at Red Emma's.

events.title: Belonging: Opening Reception
events.description: Photographs by five Baltimore photographers featured in the book In Light and Verse. Reception 6–8 p.m.; afterward the show is open by appointment through Jan. 29.

events.title: Wednesday Walk: Forest Layers
events.description: Cylburn Arboretum Friends' midday Wednesday walk, this one looking at the layers of the forest.

events.title: Lecture: Cherokee Boarding School Experiences in the Mid-Atlantic
events.venue: Maryland Center for History and Culture
events.description: David Armenti of the Maryland Center for History and Culture shares genealogical research on members of the Eastern Band of Cherokee Indians, from the Big Cove community in North Carolina, who attended boarding schools in the Chesapeake region.

events.title: CANCELLED — Isabella Weber: Anti-Fascist Economics
events.description: Economist Isabella Weber, known for her work on price controls and inflation, presents Anti-Fascist Economics: In Defense of Affordability, Dignity, and Democracy, in conversation with journalist Osita Nwanevu.
events.summary: Cancelled per Red Emma's; they may reschedule.

events.title: John Washington: How to Close a Camp
events.description: Journalist John Washington presents his book How to Close a Camp.

events.title: 50th Annual Baltimore Pow-Wow
events.description: The Baltimore American Indian Center marks its 50th anniversary with dance, performances, Indigenous food and vendors. Grand entrances at noon and 4 p.m.

events.title: Hail, Bright Cecilia: Remembering Benjamin Britten
events.description: A concert remembering the English composer Benjamin Britten, given on St. Cecilia's Day, which was also Britten's birthday.

events.title: Baltimore Museum of Industry 45th Anniversary Celebration
events.description: The BMI recreates its 1981 opening day: metalworking and printmaking demonstrations, trade demos, an oyster-shucking contest, a Baltimore trivia challenge, an '80s film in the theater and live music, with Evan Woodard of Salvage Arc as emcee.
events.summary: $1 admission all day.

events.title: Network (Senator Revival Matinee)

events.title: Screening: Fault Lines presents "Dying in Detention"
events.description: Al Jazeera's Fault Lines documentary about a man who died in an immigration detention facility in California, screened with Physicians for Human Rights and followed by a Q&A with participants and the filmmakers.
events.summary: Baltimore Magazine lists it as free.

events.title: Sade's Collective
events.description: Young jazz group with Ayomilekan Akinbinu (guitar, alto sax), Kofi Boateng (keys, trumpet), Lucas Hanson (keys) and Imran Musa, playing the early set in Keystone Korner's small room.

events.title: Cris Jacobs Family Reunion
events.description: Baltimore roots guitarist Cris Jacobs's Thanksgiving-eve reunion show, with guests from Greensky Bluegrass, Cabinet and his old band The Bridge.

events.title: Coromoto: Maria Sánchez
events.description: Photography, film and installation by Maria Sánchez exploring feminine deities, in the artist-run Current Space gallery. Open Saturdays 1-5 p.m.

events.title: Belonging: Five Baltimore Photographers
events.description: Group show of photographs from five Baltimore artists at the small Charles Village gallery Connect + Collect. Viewing by appointment.

events.title: BAZAART Holiday Market at AVAM
events.description: AVAM's annual holiday market of work by regional artists and makers, held at the visionary-art museum on Key Highway. Fri. 12-5 p.m., Sat. 10 a.m.-5 p.m.
events.summary: You're in Lima Nov 27-Dec 4.

events.title: A Christmas Carol (Chesapeake Shakespeare)

events.title: Christmas with Baltimore Choral Arts

events.summary: You're in Lima.

events.summary: You're in Lima.

events.title: Mortified Baltimore: Winter Break
events.description: Mortified's live show, where adults read their actual teenage diaries, letters and poems on stage to a roomful of strangers; the Baltimore chapter's winter edition.

events.title: Phantom Thread (Senator Revival Matinee)
events.description: Sunday-morning repeat of the Senator's revival screening of Paul Thomas Anderson's Phantom Thread (2017), with Daniel Day-Lewis as an exacting 1950s London couturier.

events.title: Maker's Night Market at Ottobar
events.description: Free maker's market on Ottobar's main floor, with local makers selling their work in the Remington rock club. Time not yet posted.

events.title: Bit Brigade: Zelda + Castlevania + Tetris Live
events.description: Bit Brigade plays the soundtracks to The Legend of Zelda, Castlevania and Tetris live as a rock band while a speedrunner plays the games on the big screen.

events.title: Handel's Messiah at the Baltimore Basilica
events.description: The complete Messiah, led by Edward Polochick with the Baltimore Basilica Festival Orchestra and Choir and soloists, in Benjamin Latrobe's 1821 Basilica, 'America's First Cathedral.'
events.summary: Also Sat Dec 12 at 7pm. Kids 12 and under free.

events.title: Station North Holiday Market

events.description: Indoor/outdoor holiday market in the Station North Arts District with 100+ Baltimore artists, makers, performers and small businesses, plus food, drink and live music.

events.title: Handel Choir of Baltimore: Messiah
events.description: The Handel Choir of Baltimore's annual Messiah, now in its 92nd season, at the Church of the Redeemer on North Charles Street (moved from Grace UMC).
events.summary: Also Dec 13, 3:30pm at Church of the Resurrection, Timonium (and livestream).

events.title: Choral Arts Chamber Singers
events.description: Baltimore Choral Arts Society's Chamber Singers in a December afternoon concert at Immanuel Lutheran Church.

events.title: Fell's Point Eggnog Tasting Tour
events.description: Fell's Point Main Street's annual eggnog tasting walk through the historic waterfront neighborhood's bars and restaurants.
events.summary: Tickets go on sale in early November.

events.title: Danielle Brown Art Opening
events.description: Opening of an art show by Danielle Brown in the upstairs bar at Ottobar.

events.title: Now, Voyager (Senator Revival Matinee)
events.description: Monday-afternoon repeat of the Senator's revival of Irving Rapper's Now, Voyager (1942), with Bette Davis as a repressed Boston heiress who blossoms after a breakdown; a classic of the sad, humane women's picture.
events.summary: Also Sun Dec 13 at 10am.

events.title: Delio Vásquez: "Huey P. Newton: I Am We"
events.description: Scholar Delio Vásquez discusses his book on Black Panther co-founder Huey P. Newton's ideas and the distortions around his legacy, in conversation with Omavi Shukur.

events.title: Victor/Victoria (Senator Revival)
events.description: Blake Edwards's 1982 musical comedy with Julie Andrews as a broke soprano in 1930s Paris who becomes a star posing as a man playing a woman; Robert Preston and James Garner co-star.

events.title: Lori Williams: An Evening of Holiday Jazz & Soul
events.description: DC-area jazz singer Lori Williams sings original jazz and soul grooves plus holiday material.

events.title: Fell's Point Cookie Crawl
events.description: Fell's Point Main Street's 6th annual cookie crawl: pick up a cookie map and bag at Su Casa Furniture (901 S Bond St) and collect cookies from shops around the neighborhood.

events.title: Sue Foley and GA-20
events.description: Texas blues guitarist Sue Foley shares a bill with Boston's GA-20, a trio playing raw, '50s-style Chicago blues. Show time not yet listed.

events.title: Makari, Kurt Travis, Mella and Resilia
events.description: All-ages post-hardcore bill at Ottobar: Makari with singer Kurt Travis, Mella and Resilia. Door time not listed.

events.title: Marc Almond – Live in Concert
events.description: Marc Almond, the voice of the British synth-pop duo Soft Cell ("Tainted Love") and a long-running solo torch singer, plays what is billed as his first-ever Lima concert.
events.summary: 21:00 per JamBase; tickets via Ticketmaster Perú (price not published in sources checked).

events.title: Los bárbaros (Javier Barbero & Martín Guerra, 2025)
events.description: Spanish-Peruvian drama (102 min): three young people from an outlying neighbourhood, with no work and no future, make a home in an abandoned half-built building and form an unlikely community — until construction restarts and they have to leave.
events.summary: Last listed screening of its run.

events.title: David Bowie: Station to Station
events.venue: Galería Earl of St Andrew's, Británico Miraflores
events.description: Exhibition tracing Bowie's reinventions from his early Shel Talmy recordings to the late 'Toy' project through photographs by Masayoshi Sukita, Mick Rock, Terry O'Neill, Brian Duffy, Andrew Kent and others, plus records and sleeves, letters, manuscripts and posters from the Perú33RPM archive. Curated by Alberto Candia.
events.summary: Mon–Sat 10:00–18:00; free. Runs Oct 29 – Dec 19.

events.title: El arte de mirarnos – 200 years of photography and dress
events.venue: Galería L'Imaginaire, Alianza Francesa de Lima
events.description: Marking 200 years of photography, curator Angela Kusen pairs archival Peruvian images with work by a new generation of Peruvian fashion photographers to look at how dressed bodies — and Peru's social and cultural changes — have been pictured across generations. French magazine Purple is a special guest.
events.summary: Gallery hours Mon–Fri 8:00–20:00, Sat 8:00–13:30; closed Sunday. Runs Nov 5 – Dec 28.

events.title: Museo Larco – pre-Columbian collection (open daily)
events.description: Lima's great private museum of ancient Peruvian art, set in an 18th-century viceregal mansion in Pueblo Libre: Moche ceramics, gold and silver work, textiles, a walk-through visible storeroom of tens of thousands of pots, and the famous erotic-ceramics gallery, surrounded by bougainvillea gardens.
events.summary: Open every day 9:00–19:00 (good for Monday, when MAC Lima and many museums close). Online tickets are discounted. Entrance on Calle Navarra.

events.title: Circuito Mágico del Agua (fountain park, nightly light shows)
events.venue: Circuito Mágico del Agua, Parque de la Reserva
events.description: A park of illuminated fountains in the 1920s Parque de la Reserva in central Lima; the Fantasía fountain show combines water, lasers and projected images after dark.
events.summary: Wed–Sun 15:00–22:00 (closed Mon & Tue); Fantasía shows 19:15, 20:15 and 21:30. Hours from a mid-2026 guide — confirm locally. Bring small bills.

events.title: Las irresponsables (Javier Daulte)
events.description: Comedy by Argentine playwright Javier Daulte: after a breakup, three friends (Claudia Berninzon, Norma Martínez, Johanna San Miguel) spend a weekend in a house and make a pact to each do something she would never do for herself. A DEA Teatro production; about 90 minutes, in Spanish.
events.summary: Teleticket lists the run Nov 5 – Dec 7; show times not published on the listing.

events.title: The Jazz Room: Un viaje al corazón de Nueva Orleans
events.description: An hour-long, 1920s-style New Orleans trad-jazz set with horns and vocals — 'St. James Infirmary', 'Basin Street Blues', 'On the Sunny Side of the Street' and other standards with room for improvisation. Performers are not named.
events.summary: Part of a Fever series running Nov 20 – Jan 22 (sessions at 18:00 and 21:00 on show nights); Nov 28 18:00 is the date confirmed in the trip window. 18+.

events.title: Bioferia de Miraflores (Saturday organic market)
events.description: Lima's long-running Saturday organic and farmers' market beside Parque Reducto No. 2 in Miraflores — produce, breads, cheeses and prepared food from small growers.
events.summary: Saturdays 8:00–14:00 per LimaEasy's guide; confirm it's on before going.

events.title: Dina Summer + Local Suicide
events.description: Dina Summer, the Berlin dark-wave/synth-pop live band project, headlines with Local Suicide — the Berlin DJ/production duo behind it, known for dark-disco sets mixing new wave, Italo, post-disco, EBM and dark techno.
events.summary: 19:00 is doors. Tickets via Passline from S/ 80.

events.title: Undercaos Resurrección 2026 (Deafkids, Hate Moss, Vinnum Sabbathi)
events.description: One-night underground festival with Brazil's DEAFKIDS (noise/psychedelic hardcore), Hate Moss (Italian-Brazilian electronic post-punk duo), Mexican stoner-doom band Vinnum Sabbathi and El Jefazo.
events.summary: Time, price and address not found; Bandsintown lists Hate Moss at 20:00 at ExpresArte academia de música.

events.title: Argy
events.description: Greek DJ/producer Argy (behind the melodic-techno hit 'Aria') plays a big-room night with cinematic visuals, supported by Peruvian DJs to be announced, promoted by Vastion.
events.summary: 22:30 per Bandsintown; tickets on the Bombo app from S/ 115. Club is in Chorrillos.

events.title: Feria del Patio – Christmas edition at MALI
events.description: The 8th edition of MALI's design and makers' market, filling the museum's patio, Gran Hall and atrium with independent design, illustration, ceramics, jewelry, local brands and food stalls, plus free workshops, talks and music.
events.summary: Dec 4–6, from 12:00 (listed until 20:00). Combine with the Pacchas and Cusco textiles exhibitions upstairs.

events.title: Mi voz es mensajera
events.description: Musical-theatre piece in Coco Llaque's 'Trilogía Criolla': sixteen original songs in the Peruvian criollo tradition sung by Mariella Fonseca, Ebelin Ortiz and María del Carmen Padilla with a live orchestra led by Agustín Rojas; written and directed by Rudy Bezir.
events.summary: Fri Dec 4 and Sat Dec 5 at 20:00; tickets on Joinnus. In Spanish.

events.title: 1st Annual Baltimore Indie Bookstore Crawl
events.description: Baltimore's first Black Friday-weekend bookstore crawl across about fifteen indie shops — Red Emma's, Normals, Greedy Reads (Remington and Fells Point), Bird in Hand, The Ivy, Atomic Books, Charm City Books and more. Visit and buy at four or more stores, then turn in your bookstore passport for a prize drawing; extra stores mean extra entries.
events.summary: Fri Nov 27 – Sun Nov 29; follow each store's own hours.

events.title: Unidos en el Arte
events.description: Group art exhibition in the galleries at Creative Alliance's Patterson building in Highlandtown.
events.summary: Gallery hours Tue–Sat 12–5 p.m.; through Dec 4.

events.title: Peabody Heights 15th Anniversary Party
events.description: Two-day party marking 15 years of Peabody Heights Brewery, the Abell brewery that hosts many of the city's DJ and drum & bass nights.
events.summary: Fri 4–11 p.m.; Sat 12–10 p.m.

events.title: Indigenous Peoples Celebration
events.address: 11201 Garrison Forest Rd, Owings Mills, MD
events.description: Free day-long celebration of Indigenous culture at Irvine Nature Center in Owings Mills, on the center's trails and grounds.

events.title: Hardcover Minibooks (bookbinding workshop)
events.description: Hands-on bookbinding workshop at Creative Alliance where you make two miniature hardcover books.

events.title: Highlandtown Holiday Night Market
events.description: Evening holiday market of handmade goods from local artists and vendors, hosted at Creative Alliance in Highlandtown.

events.title: Painted Screens: A Baltimore Folk Art (workshop)
events.description: Workshop on Baltimore's painted window-screen tradition, the rowhouse folk art of East Baltimore; you finish by painting a small screen to take home.

events.title: Bluegrass Nutcracker
events.description: Creative Alliance's featured holiday show: Tchaikovsky's Nutcracker reworked as a bluegrass performance.

events.title: Candlelight Carols & Organ Recital
events.description: Emmanuel's annual Festival of Lessons and Carols, directed by Christian Lane: a holiday organ recital, then a candlelit service of carols and readings by the Emmanuel Choir and guest readers in the Mount Vernon church.
events.summary: Free reservations encouraged.

events.title: Christian Sands Trio: Christmas Stories
events.description: Pianist Christian Sands, a five-time Grammy nominee who has played with Wynton Marsalis, Dianne Reeves and Yo-Yo Ma, leads his trio through a cinematic take on holiday standards.
